\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{বাথরুম} (bāthrum)}{বাথরুম (bāthrum)}]{\bn{বাথরুম} (bāthrum) — a bathroom}

\label{lesson:BN-C405-bathrum}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for to rest a while, then the Bengali for to lean back.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{বাথরুম}}
\textbf{\bn{বাথরুম}} — \emph{bāthrum} — \textquotedblleft{}a bathroom\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{আমাদের} \bn{ঘরের} \bn{বাথরুমে} \bn{গরম} \bn{জল} \bn{আছে।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{āmāder ghôrer bāthrume gôrôm jôl āchhe.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
There is hot water in our room's bathroom.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{বাথরুম}} (\emph{bāthrum}) is borrowed from English \emph{bathroom}; the English th is said with \bn{থ}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bāthrum}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bāthrum}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{āmāder ghôrer bāthrume gôrôm jôl āchhe.} — There is hot water in our room's bathroom.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for to rest a while, then the Bengali for to lean back, then say \emph{bāthrum} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \bn{বাথরুম} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A bathroom\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{টয়লেট} (ṭôyleṭ)}{টয়লেট (ṭôyleṭ)}]{\bn{টয়লেট} (ṭôyleṭ) — a toilet}

\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for to lean back, then the Bengali for a bathroom.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{গিজার} (gijār)}{গিজার (gijār)}]{\bn{গিজার} (gijār) — a water heater; a geyser}

\label{lesson:BN-C405-gijar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for a bathroom, then the Bengali for a toilet.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{গিজার}}
\textbf{\bn{গিজার}} — \emph{gijār} — \textquotedblleft{}a water heater; a geyser\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{গিজারটা} \bn{চালু} \bn{করলে} \bn{গরম} \bn{জল} \bn{পাবে।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{gijārṭā chālu kôrle gôrôm jôl pābe.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Switch on the water heater and you will get hot water.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{গিজার}} (\emph{gijār}) is borrowed from English \emph{geyser}, the Indian English name for a water heater in a bathroom, from the hot springs of Iceland.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for a bathroom, then the Bengali for a toilet, then say \emph{gijār} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{এসি} (esi)}{এসি (esi)}]{\bn{এসি} (esi) — an air conditioner}

\label{lesson:BN-C405-esi}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for a toilet, then the Bengali for a water heater.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{এসি}}
\textbf{\bn{এসি}} — \emph{esi} — \textquotedblleft{}an air conditioner\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{গরমে} \bn{আমরা} \bn{এসি} \bn{চালিয়ে} \bn{ঘুমালাম।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{gôrôme āmrā esi chāliye ghumālām.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
In the heat we slept with the air conditioner on.
\end{quote}

Said as the two English letters A C.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{এসি}} (\emph{esi}) is borrowed from English \emph{AC}, the letters of \emph{air conditioning}, said as a word.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{esi}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{esi}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{gôrôme āmrā esi chāliye ghumālām.} — In the heat we slept with the air conditioner on.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for a toilet, then the Bengali for a water heater, then say \emph{esi} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{পরিষ্কার} \bn{করা} (pôrishkār kôrā)}{পরিষ্কার করা (pôrishkār kôrā)}]{\bn{পরিষ্কার} \bn{করা} (pôrishkār kôrā) — to clean}

\label{lesson:BN-C405-porishkar-kora}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for a water heater, then the Bengali for an air conditioner.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{পরিষ্কার} \bn{করা}}
\textbf{\bn{পরিষ্কার} \bn{করা}} — \emph{pôrishkār kôrā} — \textquotedblleft{}to clean\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{সকালে} \bn{হোটেলের} \bn{কর্মী} \bn{আমাদের} \bn{ঘর} \bn{পরিষ্কার} \bn{করলেন।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{sôkāle hoṭeler kôrmī āmāder ghôr pôrishkār kôrlen.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
In the morning the hotel worker cleaned our room.
\end{quote}

Past (he/she …): \bn{তিনি} \bn{ঘর} \bn{পরিষ্কার} \bn{করলেন}, \emph{tini ghôr pôrishkār kôrlen}.

\bn{পরিষ্কার} alone is the adjective clean, clear: \bn{পরিষ্কার} \bn{জল}, clean water; \bn{পরিষ্কার} \bn{আকাশ}, a clear sky.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{পরিষ্কার} \bn{করা}} (\emph{pôrishkār kôrā}) joins Sanskrit \emph{pariṣkāra}, \textquotedblleft{}preparing, adorning, making fit\textquotedblright{} (Monier-Williams), to \bn{করা}, to do; Bengali settled on making clean.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{pôrishkār kôrā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{pôrishkār kôrā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sôkāle hoṭeler kôrmī āmāder ghôr pôrishkār kôrlen.} — In the morning the hotel worker cleaned our room.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for a water heater, then the Bengali for an air conditioner, then say \emph{pôrishkār kôrā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
